steps.name: Replace the noise denylist with positional card extraction (REFACTOR)
criteria: Extraction is positional per DR-0008: split the block into runs of consecutive non-blank lines, find the run holding the job link, and take that run's lines before the link as the card when there are 3 or more, otherwise the immediately preceding run; the triple is the card's first three lines.
TRAILING_NOISE_LINE is deleted, not retained-but-unused, for every pattern except the salary line.
The salary pattern is retained only because the per-card salary is captured and its line must be recognised to be read — not as a skip-list entry.

All 7 existing scenarios in tests/regression/job-alert-harvester/linkedin-block-anchor.test.mjs stay green, unmodified — they pin the three historical leaks and are the evidence the positional rule subsumes the denylist.
A full corpus rebuild produces byte-identical Jobs rows to the current build: 146 jobs, 102 companies, 7 saved searches, zero changed title/company/location values.
Per-card salary capture and canonical link reconstruction are unaffected.
steps.scenario_name: existing scenarios pin the behaviour; this step changes mechanism, not output
steps.implementation_notes: Read docs/decisions/DR-0008-card-position-not-a-noise-denylist.md first — it carries the rule, the four observed block shapes, and why the >= 3 discriminator exists. This is a REFACTOR: behaviour is already pinned by 7 regression scenarios plus the walking skeleton, and the corpus output must not change at all. Measured before briefing: the positional rule agrees with the current three-patch denylist parser on 198 of 198 cards, 0 disagreements. Shapes 2/3 (noise in the link's run, so the preceding run wins) and shape 4 (preamble in the preceding run, triple at the head of the link's run, so the prefix wins) pull in opposite directions — the >= 3 test is what separates them; do not simplify it away. Keep cardSalary/parseCardSalaryLine and the job.rate surface intact (steps 01-05 and 01-06 of fix-linkedin-header-shift). src/core/ stays pure: no classes, no mutation, no node: imports. Prefer a declarative pipeline over an index-walking loop — the backward walk this replaces was the last imperative holdout in the module.

steps.name: Assert every job link yields a row, and refuse when one does not (RED+GREEN)
criteria: extractJobs compares the number of lines carrying a /jobs/view/ link against the number of rows it emits, and throws naming the message id and both counts when they differ.
The error message says which message and how many cards were lost, so the failure is diagnosable without re-running a probe.
The CLI --in branch catches it and refuses before writing: non-zero exit, nothing written to --out, no stack trace.
A well-formed message is unaffected — the assertion is silent on all 70 messages across .cache/messages and fixtures/linkedin*, where links and rows both total 255.
extract still returns an array, per DR-0006 rule 1 — the assertion must not change the descriptor's return shape.
All existing tests stay green: regression 7/7, walking skeleton 8/8, suite unchanged at 100 passed / 16 failed / 1 skipped.
steps.scenario_name: a job link whose card cannot be read refuses the run instead of vanishing
steps.implementation_notes: Closes the contradiction recorded in DR-0008 (card position, not a noise denylist), whose Exceptions section claims a broken positional rule 'should break loudly — a card with fewer than three lines yields no row'. Yielding no row IS the silence: jobAtLine returns null at parse-linkedin.mjs:127 and parseBlockJobs's .filter(Boolean) discards it with no count or warning. A vanished row is worse than the shifted rows this feature fixed, because a shifted row at least appears in the sheet where an audit catches it. Also contradicts DR-0006 rule 2 (unmatched input captured, never dropped), which is already implemented for messages at sources/registry.mjs:21 returning {rows, unmatched} and for truncated payloads via slim.mjs quarantine — the job level is the one place the pattern is missing. Count LINES matching JOB_ID_IN_URL, not raw regex occurrences: jobAtLine takes only the first match per line, so a hypothetical two-links-on-one-line would otherwise read as a false drop. Both counts are 255 today. Expected count is derived from the input, so unlike DR-0003's ingest --expect nobody can supply it wrongly. TRADE-OFF ACCEPTED: throwing aborts the whole rebuild over one malformed message, losing the other good rows for that run. Chosen deliberately — DR-0001 makes rebuild cheap and repeatable from cache, so nothing is lost permanently, whereas a partial sheet is wrong until someone notices.
